messages:
omar-partnerships: hey @rachel-stratus — quick ask. we’re updating the cost model for Dedicated pools and need StratusGrid inputs for reserved vs ephemeral (spot) pricing.
Can you share a CSV (region, sku, gpu_type, reserved_price_per_hour, reserved_commit_months, spot_price_per_hour, avg_eviction_rate_pct, spot_slippage_pct, upfront_pct, notes)?
Specifically we need: per-gpu vs per-instance semantics, whether reserved price includes any egress/network, commit-tenor discounts, and a suggested cross-region correlation factor for spot evictions. ideally by region + sku. thx!

rachel-stratus: hi Omar — uploaded a concise CSV and pasted a small snippet below. full full sheet is on the partner portal: https://partners.stratusgrid.example/sheets/SG-pricing-2026 (access: redwood-partners@).

```csv
region,sku,gpu_type,reserved_price_per_hour,reserved_commit_months,spot_price_per_hour,avg_eviction_rate_pct,spot_slippage_pct,upfront_pct,notes
us-west-1,SG-A100-80GB,A100-80GB,2.50,12,0.95,5,8,20,reserved per-GPU; network egress excluded
us-east-1,SG-H100-80GB,H100-80GB,5.00,12,1.60,7,12,25,reserved per-instance (4 GPUs/inst)
eu-central-1,SG-A100-40GB,A100-40GB,1.40,6,0.60,10,15,15,min burst 10 nodes
``` 

Notes: reserved_price is the hourly rate after commit discount (no egress). upfront_pct is typical down payment we can offer (applies to 6/12/24-tenors). spot_slippage_pct = observed price volatility when capacity tightens (use this for modeling per-token cost uplift). avg_eviction is the historical mean over last 90 days.

stratus-bot: File uploaded: SG-pricing-2026.csv (shared to #partnerships)

jess-product: thanks Rachel. clarification: for H100 row — reserved is per-instance (4 GPUs). for cost model we prefer per-GPU normalised numbers. can you confirm instance size so we can divide? also does the reserved price include reserved NVMe for caching or is storage billed separately?

rachel-stratus: good q — H100 instances are 4x H100 (so divide by 4 to get per-GPU). NVMe cache is extra; we bill storage separately (we expose a packaged discount if you commit >100 instances/month). i can add a column for storage_rate_per_hour in the full CSV.

liam-finance: can you also add a field for 'billing_mode' (hourly vs monthly fixed vs upfront credit) + a simple amortized monthly cost assuming 12-mo commit and 20% upfront? that helps our capex amortization calc.

rachel-stratus: yep will add billing_mode + sample amortized_monthly_usd for 6/12/24 tenors. quick note: our "upfront_pct" in the CSV is what we recommend; finance teams often negotiate higher for deeper discounts.

sophia-ops: two operational asks: 1) is spot availability correlated across AZs in a region (do evictions happen region-wide)? 2) for burst capacity, do you guarantee minimum burst or is that opportunistic?

rachel-stratus: ops answer: 1) partial correlation — hardware maintenance and large tenant reclaim events can cause multi-AZ evaporation. for modeling assume a 15% cross-AZ correlation factor (i.e., independent eviction probability -> adjust upward by ~15% for correlated events). 2) burst is not guaranteed; we offer a soft-minimum 'min_burst' when you sign a commit >X, but it's throttled during peak. i'll flag min_burst in the sheet for relevant skus.

jess-product: perfect. for our baseline ingest we'll normalise everything to per-GPU hourly, add storage and egress rows, and run base-case: 60% reserved(12mo) / 40% spot. can the CSV include a suggested recommended split (partner_recommendation_split)? some partners give guidance and we sometimes track that.

rachel-stratus: added partner_recommendation_split column: default for Redwood use-case = "70/30 reserved/spot for latency-sensitive + burst patterns". also put a note: "if cost-first workloads -> 50/50 or higher spot".

omar-partnerships: awesome, thanks all. next steps: Rachel—we'll ingest the CSV into the cost model this afternoon. Finance will run sensitivity on eviction +/-10pp and spot_slippage +/-5pp. Ops will model a 15% cross-AZ correlation factor. we'll follow up if we need per-rack vulnerability curves. :thumbsup:

liam-finance: one ask — can you also include typical invoice lag (days) and whether reserved discounts are prorated mid-cycle? that affects our cashflow timing model.

rachel-stratus: will add invoice_lag_days and prorate_policy. short answers: invoice_lag=7–14 days typical, prorate mid-cycle = yes for instance scale-down, no refund for early termination without penalty clauses.

omar-partnerships: great, sending a short doc with how we'll map columns to our model. I'll post back with ingest results and baseline unit costs. thanks Rachel :raised_hands:

sophia-ops: tagging @eng-sre for visibility — some of these slippage/eviction assumptions will feed routing/fallback policies.

rachel-stratus: thanks — ping me if you want a time to walk through the sheet live. can do a 30m sync tomorrow PST.
